troubleshooting.problem: The sauce darkens while a thigh is still below 165°F
troubleshooting.cause: The coating receives more direct broiler heat than the center.
troubleshooting.fix: Use a less intense broiler setting or a lower rack position permitted by the oven, turn as needed and continue cooking to the measured endpoint. Do not treat a dark surface as proof of doneness.

after.storage: Store cooked chicken separately from rolls, pickles and fried onions. Refrigerate in shallow containers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C; keep at 40°F / 4°C or colder and use within 3–4 days. Reheat chicken to 165°F / 74°C throughout before rebuilding sliders. Toast the rolls separately; fried onions lose their crunch against wet sauce.
after.timing: For the original batch in one chicken load, plan roughly 20 minutes of hands-on preparation and assembly, 30 minutes refrigerated marinating and about 20 minutes of broiling and resting, with some overlap. Allow about 1 hour 15 minutes overall. A longer marinade or extra chicken/roll loads extend elapsed time; the 5-minute chicken rest can overlap roll toasting.

exactBodyChange.before:
## Chef's Note

The difference between good and great sliders is building flavor at every step. Marinating the thighs in BBQ sauce with smoked paprika for even 30 minutes infuses flavor deep into the meat - don't skip this. Broiling chars the edges and caramelizes the sugars in the sauce. Sharp cheddar melted on top adds richness, pickles cut through with acid, and crispy fried onions bring texture. Brush the Hawaiian rolls with melted butter and toast them cut-side down in the oven while the chicken rests - this takes 2 minutes and makes a huge difference.

## Directions

1. **Marinate:** Toss chicken thighs with 1/3 cup BBQ sauce, olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Let sit 30 minutes at room temperature (or up to 4 hours refrigerated).

2. **Broil:** Position rack 6 inches from broiler. Remove chicken from marinade, shake off excess. Broil on a sheet pan for 6-7 minutes per side until charred and cooked through (165°F).

3. **Glaze & Cheese:** Brush hot chicken generously with remaining BBQ sauce. Top each thigh with cheddar. Broil 1-2 more minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly.

4. **Toast Rolls:** While chicken rests, brush cut sides of Hawaiian rolls with melted butter. Place cut-side down on a sheet pan and toast under broiler for 1-2 minutes until golden.

5. **Slice:** Let chicken rest 5 minutes. Slice into slider-sized pieces.

6. **Assemble:** Add chicken with melted cheese to toasted rolls. Top with pickles and crispy fried onions. Serve with extra BBQ sauce.
exactBodyChange.after:
## Chef's Note

BBQ sauce, smoked paprika and garlic coat the thighs before broiling; reserve a clean share of sauce for the glaze. The cheese and buttered rolls keep these sliders rich, while pickles and fried onions add tang and crunch. Watch the sauce and bread closely under the broiler: their sugars can darken before the chicken is ready.

## Directions

1. **Marinate in the refrigerator:** Toss boneless skinless chicken thighs, 1/3 of the BBQ sauce, olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, kosher salt, and black pepper together, using one-third of the measured BBQ sauce and leaving the other two-thirds in a clean container for glazing. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours. Keep the clean sauce and utensils away from the raw chicken.
2. **Broil the thighs:** Set up a broiler-safe metal sheet pan and use the rack position permitted by the oven, about 6 inches below the broiler where the oven instructions permit. Lift the thighs from the marinade, shake off excess and discard the used marinade. Arrange in a single layer without overlap; cook in additional loads if necessary. Start checking at 6–7 minutes per side, turning as the surface browns. Check the thickest part of each thigh with a thermometer and continue until each reaches 165°F / 74°C. Watch sugary spots closely rather than waiting for heavy blackening. Move cooked chicken with clean utensils.
3. **Glaze and melt the cheese:** Use 2/3 of the BBQ sauce and sharp cheddar slices for the glaze and topping: brush the cooked thighs with the clean reserved sauce, then distribute all the cheese halves evenly over the chicken. The number of thighs need not equal the number of rolls. Broil for about 1–2 minutes, watching until the cheese melts; remove before the sauce burns.
4. **Rest the chicken and toast the rolls:** Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, use Hawaiian rolls and butter for the rolls: brush their cut faces with all the melted butter. Put the rolls cut-side up on a clean broiler-safe sheet pan and watch for 1–2 minutes, removing them as soon as the cut faces are golden.
5. **Slice and assemble:** Divide all the rested chicken and melted cheese into one bun-sized portion for each measured roll. Add dill pickle chips, crispy fried onions, and additional BBQ sauce to the sliders and serve while the rolls and onions are crisp.
